- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If 3+ consecutive days of downward sentiment, model underreacts; add 0.5–1.0 to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Mean reversion bias: if 5+ consecutive days of price movement > ±2% from 30-day average, adjust forecast toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–3 days; if sentiment is trending, add 0.5–1.0 to forecast to account for momentum.
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.15+ swings in 3 days), reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overfitting to noise.
